A LEADER IN GLOBAL HEALTH & INFECTIOUS DISEASES
SIGA is a leader in global health, developing medicines to prevent and treat emerging infectious diseases with high unmet medical needs.

Infectious diseases pose an imminent and severe threat to global health that cannot be adequately addressed with vaccines alone. Smallpox is particularly worrisome because it is highly infectious and deadly. We are developing best-in-class products to treat this infection in patients worldwide. Society must take proactive steps to prevent and stop outbreaks – whether natural, accidental, or intentional. We are committed to partnering with governments, commercial organizations, foundations, and others who share responsibility for global health security.

Our experienced, multidisciplinary team has a profound passion for innovation and public health advancement.

As the threat of smallpox looms, our team is steadfast in its goal of ensuring governments and other key stakeholders are equipped with medicines and other countermeasures to combat devastating diseases. By preparing for the unthinkable, we help build a resilient defense against a devastating outbreak. We are committed to safeguarding your health which preserves your peace of mind through our collective proactive and unwavering efforts.
Countries in which Products are Sold
We are equipped to respond rapidly to a smallpox outbreak, collaborating with healthcare professionals, governments, and communities to minimize the spread and impact on people.

Global cooperation is essential to prevent and stop infectious disease outbreaks. Our rich history of successful partnerships with over 30 countries and many organizations enables an extensive reach across multiple stakeholders to combat a smallpox outbreak. Additionally, the U.S. government has relied on our TPOXX treatment for over a decade to equip the Strategic National Stockpile (SNS) against a potential smallpox outbreak.
TPOXX® (tecovirimat) is a best-in-class product franchise

TPOXX is a highly targeted antiviral with a strong safety profile. It prevents viral particles from exiting the cell in which they are produced, thereby slowing the spread of infection, and allowing the patient’s immune system to clear the virus.

Oral TPOXX was the first U.S. FDA-approved antiviral treatment for smallpox. It is also available in an IV formulation. In Canada, oral TPOXX is approved for the same indication. In the EU, as well as Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein, TPOXX, known as Tecovirimat SIGA, is approved for the treatment of smallpox, cowpox, and vaccinia complications following vaccination against smallpox. In the UK and Japan, under the brand names Tecovirimat SIGA and TEPOXX, respectively, the antiviral is approved for the treatment of orthopoxvirus infections, including mpox, smallpox, cowpox, and vaccinia complications following vaccination against smallpox.

Additionally, we are working to advance regulatory approval for TPOXX in new indications and formulations, including as a post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for smallpox, and a pediatric formulation for the treatment of smallpox.
